topic: Hotel aggregator system design — how a platform that searches many hotel suppliers, each returning completely different JSON, uses one adapter per supplier, a canonical model and a master hotel ID to show one comparable price per hotel.

title.sub: Every hotel supplier speaks its own dialect.

stages.title: Three suppliers, three JSONs
stages.desc: The same room, described three ways: per night, in paise, in dollars.
stages.status: Supplier A · B · C · one Goa resort
stages.narration: One hotel in Goa. Three suppliers. Three completely different JSON shapes.

stages.title: Used as-is
stages.desc: No adapter in the middle. Supplier C says 212.40 USD, and the app shows ₹212.
stages.status: USD read as rupees · top of the list
stages.narration: Show the JSON as-is, and dollars become rupees. A two hundred rupee resort.

stages.title: The quiet bug
stages.desc: Supplier B sends paise. Nobody divided by 100, so its hotels sank out of sight.
stages.narration: The quiet bug: paise shown as rupees, a hundred times too high.

stages.title: One hotel, three listings
stages.desc: Three names, three IDs, one building. The list shows it three times.
stages.narration: And the same resort appears three times, under three different names.

stages.title: One adapter per supplier
stages.desc: Each adapter knows one supplier: its auth, its JSON, its units, its quirks.
stages.status: Adapter A · Adapter B · Adapter C
stages.narration: The fix: one adapter per supplier, in between the JSON and your app.

stages.title: One canonical model
stages.desc: Whole stay, taxes in, major units, ISO currency. Every adapter returns the same shape.
stages.status: total · taxes in · INR · UTC deadlines
stages.narration: Every adapter returns one model: total stay price, taxes included, one currency.

stages.title: One master hotel ID
stages.desc: An offline mapping turns three supplier IDs into one hotel, with three offers.
stages.narration: A master hotel ID merges the three listings into one hotel, three offers.

stages.title: A slow supplier? Budget
stages.desc: Call every adapter at once. At 2.5 seconds, cancel whoever is still running.
stages.status: fan out in parallel · 2.5 s budget
stages.narration: Call every supplier at once, under a time budget. Slow ones drop out.

stages.title: The JSON changes
stages.desc: Supplier B renames a field overnight. Its adapter rejects and counts. Search carries on.
stages.narration: When a supplier changes its JSON, the adapter rejects, counts, and alerts you.

stages.title: Every JSON in, one model out
stages.desc: Adapters per supplier, one canonical model, one master hotel ID, one time budget.
stages.narration: Every JSON in. One model out.

end.title: Every JSON in. One model out.
end.sub: One adapter per supplier, one canonical model, one master hotel ID, and a time budget on every search.

post.caption:
A hotel aggregator does not fail on search. It fails on translation. 🏨

Picture three hotel suppliers returning the same Goa resort:
• Supplier A: price per night, taxes extra
• Supplier B: total per stay, in paise
• Supplier C: total in US dollars, fee at the hotel

Show that JSON as it arrives and you get a ₹212 resort at the top of the list, the same hotel three times, and a 9-second search.

THE DESIGN
1. One adapter per supplier. Auth, JSON, units and quirks stop there.
2. One canonical model: total for the stay, taxes in, major units, ISO currency, UTC deadlines.
3. One master hotel ID, mapped offline by distance and name score, with a review queue.
4. Fan out to every supplier in parallel under a 2.5-second budget. A slow one drops out.
5. Archive raw responses, replay them in tests, and alert when an adapter starts rejecting offers.

Search prices can be cached for minutes. The price a traveller pays is always re-checked with the supplier.

The payloads in this short are illustrative shapes, not any supplier's real contract.

Full system design write-up: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/hotel-aggregator-system-design-supplier-integration

Follow for system design and cloud engineering tips.
